response.sql: WITH per_event AS (SELECT link_to_event AS event_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM attendance WHERE link_to_event IS NOT NULL GROUP BY link_to_event), total AS (SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total_cnt FROM per_event), shares AS (SELECT p.event_id, p.cnt, CAST(p.cnt AS REAL) / t.total_cnt AS share FROM per_event p CROSS JOIN total t WHERE t.total_cnt IS NOT NULL), ranked AS (SELECT event_id, cnt, share, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY share DESC NULLS LAST) AS rk FROM shares) SELECT event_id, cnt, share FROM ranked WHERE rk <= 10 ORDER BY share DESC NULLS LAST, event_id;

assumptions.assumption: The total is the number of attendance rows whose link_to_event is not NULL, i.e. the sum of the per-event counts. Rows with a NULL event id are excluded from both the per-event groups and the total, and event ids need not exist in the event table.
Ties are handled with RANK() over share, so every event whose share equals the 10th-highest share is kept. If the total is NULL (no attendance rows), the query returns no rows.
